newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares off but may spark up on new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares off but may spark up on new cabinet.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on Friday as domestic operators took profits and foreign investors refused to rise to the bait of lower prices, traders said.
But some traders said the market could perk up next week, rising slightly if President Boris Yeltsin announces a reformist cabinet as expected, on Monday or Tuesday.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index fell 1.5 percent to 329.37 from 334.48 on Thursday on a relatively low $32.3 million total market volume.

Shares of national electric utility UES fell to $0.2256 from $0.2315 at Thursday's close, LUKoil oil producer dropped to $14.30 from $14.51 and Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS oil company eased to $0.840 from $0.854.
Top gainers, reflecting a recent trend, were dominated by less well known shares such as regional power utility Kubanenergo which jumped to $18.80 from $16.90.
"The market is openly weak," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze, though he predicted Yeltsin's appointments would cause shares to firm.
"Next week should produce some good news, which will be reason for speculation," he said.
Peter Kizenko, chief equity trader at ING Barings said Thursday's 160-point plunge in the Dow Jones average had put the brakes on the Russian market.
"American investors are distracted by their own problems, though London is also inactive," he said.
Second tiers were the only thing Westerners were buying, he said. "For foreign investors there is little on this market to spark interest."
